title: John McDowell's forensic assessment of the bodies

tellings.quote: There is evidence, there's data to show that some of these bodies, these entities, can be interpreted to be perhaps living organisms.
McDowell saw the bodies in person. He was joined by Jim Caruso, the chief medical examiner for Denver and a forensic pathologist.
tellings.difference: Adds that McDowell saw the bodies in person and that Jim Caruso, Denver's chief medical examiner, was with him.
tellings.link_reason: This is the same McDowell–Caruso forensic examination of the bodies that telling 8 gives in McDowell's own words, now told by the host.

as_told.title: McDowell and Caruso examine the bodies in person

plain: A forensic investigator named John McDowell says there is data showing that some of the small, three-fingered bodies found in Peru 'can be interpreted to be perhaps living organisms,' rather than objects that were made. McDowell gives this as his own assessment, and Michels adds that McDowell saw the bodies in person, joined by Jim Caruso, Denver's chief medical examiner and a forensic pathologist. If true, it would mean the bodies were once living beings.
